spans.s:
maunī-amāvāsyā
(‘the new-मोओन् day of mauna [or observing silence]’)
------------------------------------------
The अमावास्या during the month of Māgha, is called ‘maunī अमावास्या’. On this day people are advised to keep mauna or observe silence or behave like munis or sages, observing spiritual disciplines like सत्य or speaking the truth, ब्रह्मचर्य or celibacy and so on. However, this day is held to be extremely auspicious to have a dip in the Saṅgama or Triveṇīsaṅgama, the confluence of the rivers गङ्गा, यमुना and the subterranean सरस्वती of Vedic fame, situated in प्रयाग or the modern Allahabad (in Uttar Pradesh). Every year lakhs of people gather on the banks of the rivers गङ्गा and यमुना at Allahabad during the month of Māgha (January) and the religious fair goes by the name ‘Māghamelā’. Once in 12 years is held the biggest religious fair of the whole world, called ‘Kumbhamelā’.
